# Rādha Saṁyutta (SN 23)

**ID:** SN 23
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Rādha Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0303m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

According to the commentary (*Sāratthappakāsinī*), the Buddha favored Rādha when expounding subtle and profound topics [Bodhi 2000]. Prominent teachings in the collection include the exposition that the goal of dispassion is liberation (SN 23.1) [Anālayo 2019], the allegory in the *Sattasutta* (SN 23.2) of children dismantling their toy sandcastles as an image for dismantling and abandoning craving for the aggregates [Yinshun 2004], and the allegorical identification of Māra not as a personal mythological tempter, but with the five aggregates and all perishable phenomena (SN 23.1, SN 23.11–12) [Dayal 1932].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- This file contains 13 suttas; 13 of them have known parallels. Full parallels by collection: SĀ (10), Pali (1)
- Examples of full non-Pali parallels: SN 23.1 Mārasutta ↔ SA 120 魔; SN 23.2 Sattasutta ↔ SA 122 眾生; SN 23.4 Pariññeyyasutta ↔ SA 112 斷知; SN 23.9 Chandarāgasutta ↔ SA 77 貪; sn23.9-10 ↔ SA 123 愛喜貪; SN 23.11 Mārasutta ↔ SA 124 魔; SN 23.12 Māradhammasutta ↔ SA 121 死法; sn23.19-22 ↔ SA 127 斷法; sn23.23 ↔ SA 125 魔所作; sn23.24 ↔ SA 126 死法

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2000] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Samyutta Nikāya (2000) — Details on structure (four vaggas, 46 suttas), commentary notes, and doctrinal character as an appendix to SN 22.
- [Williams 2000] Paul Williams, Buddhism: Critical Concepts in Religious Studies, Vol. 4: Madhyamaka (2000) — PTS volume and page span (S III 188-200) and aggregate focus.
- [Dayal 1932] Har Dayal, The Bodhisattva Doctrine in Buddhist Sanskrit Literature (1932) — Discussion of the allegorical/impersonal equation of Māra with the five aggregates in SN 23.
- [Yinshun 2004] Yinshun, Investigations into Śūnyatā (transl.) — Citation of SN 23.2 (Sattasutta) on dismantling the aggregates.
- [Anālayo 2019] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mindfulness of Breathing: A Practice Guide and Translations (2019) — Citation of SN 23.1 regarding dispassion leading to liberation.
